title: Pork Slaughtering Procedures in the Dirty Area including Scalding, Singeing, Scraping and Shaving

lessons.title: What the dirty area is and why it is kept apart
lessons.html:
The dirty area in a pork abattoir

A pork abattoir is divided into a dirty area and a clean area. The dirty area is where the pig still has its skin, hair, dirt and dung on the outside. Here the pig is stunned, stuck and bled, then scalded, de-haired, singed, scraped and shaved. The clean area starts after the outside of the carcass is clean. That is where the belly is opened and the guts are taken out.

The two areas are kept apart because dirt and germs on the skin can make meat unsafe. If a worker walks from the dirty area into the clean area with dirty boots, apron or knife, he carries germs onto clean meat. This is called cross-contamination.

Rules for working in the dirty area

  • Wear the colour of clothing your abattoir gives to dirty-area workers. Many plants use a different colour for each area so that supervisors can see who belongs where.
  • Stay in your own area. If you must go to the clean area, follow the plant rule: change apron, wash hands and boots, and sterilise knives.
  • Keep your knife in the sterilizer when you are not cutting.
  • Do not let carcasses touch the floor, walls or each other.
  • Tell your supervisor at once if a carcass falls or gets dirty.

The order of work

  1. Pigs come from the lairage (holding pens) to the stunning box.
  2. The pig is stunned so that it feels no pain.
  3. The pig is stuck (a cut to the big blood vessels near the heart) and bled.
  4. The carcass is scalded in hot water to loosen the hair.
  5. The de-hairing machine or workers remove most of the hair.
  6. The carcass is singed with a flame to burn off fine hair.
  7. Workers scrape and shave off the last hair and burnt skin.
  8. The carcass is washed and goes to the clean area.

Every step must be done well. A badly scalded pig is hard to de-hair. A badly shaved pig may be trimmed or rejected by the meat inspector. That means less money for the abattoir and for the farmer.

lessons.title: Scalding and de-hairing
lessons.html:
Scalding

After bleeding, the pig carcass goes into a scalding tank filled with hot water, or through a scalding tunnel with hot water spray or steam. The heat loosens the hair roots and the top layer of skin (the scurf) so that they come off easily.

Why time and temperature matter

  • If the water is too cold or the time is too short, the hair stays tight. The de-hairer cannot remove it and workers must scrape for a long time.
  • If the water is too hot or the time is too long, the skin cooks. It tears and becomes dark, and the carcass may need trimming.

Your abattoir has a set water temperature and scalding time. Follow your plant procedure and check the thermometer as you were trained. Report any change to your supervisor. Do not change settings on your own.

Keeping the scald water clean

Scald water gets dirty from dung, mud and blood. Dirty water spreads germs. Pigs must be bled out well before scalding, and the tank is drained and cleaned as the plant schedule says.

De-hairing

After scalding, the carcass goes into the de-hairing machine (dehairer). Rubber paddles or scrapers turn the carcass and rub off most of the hair. Watch for:

  • Carcasses that come out with patches of hair. This often means the scald was not right.
  • Torn skin or broken legs. Report this.
  • Hair and water building up around the machine. Keep the area clean.

Safety

  • Hot water and steam burn. Never put your hands into the scald tank.
  • Never reach into the de-hairer while it runs. Switch off and lock out before you clear a blockage, and only if you are trained and allowed to.
  • Floors are wet and greasy. Wear non-slip boots.

lessons.title: Singeing, scraping and shaving
lessons.html:
Singeing

After de-hairing, fine hairs are still left on the skin. The carcass is hung on the rail by the hind legs (on a gambrel) and passes through a singeing furnace or is singed with a hand-held gas burner. The flame burns off fine hair and also kills many germs on the skin. It makes the skin firm.

  • Move the flame evenly. Do not hold it in one place, or the skin will burn black.
  • Pay attention to hard places: the head, ears, armpits, between the legs and around the feet.

Gas burner safety

  • Check hoses and fittings for leaks before use. Never use a damaged hose.
  • Never point the flame at another person.
  • Keep gas bottles upright and away from heat.
  • Know where the fire extinguisher is.
  • If you smell gas, turn the valve off and tell your supervisor.

Scraping and shaving

After singeing, workers scrape the carcass with a scraper or the back of a knife to remove burnt hair and black skin. Then they shave any hairs left with a sharp knife. Work from the top of the carcass downwards, so that dirt falls away from clean skin.

  • Hold the knife flat. Do not cut into the skin or fat.
  • Rinse the knife and put it in the sterilizer often.
  • Check the whole carcass: ears, eyelids, snout, feet, the tail area.

After shaving, the carcass is washed with clean water. The carcass is then checked. It must be free of hair, scurf and dirt before it goes to the clean area. If it is not clean, it goes back for more work. Never send a dirty carcass on to save time.

Key points

  • The dirty area and clean area are kept apart to stop cross-contamination.
  • Scalding loosens hair; wrong time or temperature causes poor de-hairing or cooked skin.
  • Never reach into the de-hairer while it is running.
  • Singe evenly, and handle gas burners safely.
  • Scrape and shave from top to bottom and sterilise your knife often.
  • Only a clean, hair-free carcass may go into the clean area.

quiz.question: Why is the dirty area kept apart from the clean area?

options.text: To make the work go faster
To stop germs and dirt from the skin reaching clean meat
Because the law says pigs must be weighed there

quiz.question: What is the main purpose of scalding a pig carcass?

options.text: To loosen the hair and scurf

quiz.question: What happens if the scald water is too hot or the time is too long?

options.text: The skin cooks, tears and may need trimming

quiz.question: The de-hairing machine is blocked. What must you do?

options.text: Reach in quickly while it runs
Switch off and lock out first, and only clear it if you are trained and allowed

quiz.question: In which direction should you scrape and shave a hanging carcass?
Singeing burns off fine hair and also kills many germs on the skin.
If you are running late, you may send a carcass with some hair on it to the clean area.
Which are safe practices when using a gas singeing burner? (select all that apply)

options.text: Check hoses and fittings for leaks before use
Point the flame at a co-worker to dry his apron
Know where the fire extinguisher is
Keep gas bottles upright and away from heat
Use a cracked hose if it still works
